title: About
text:
What is SoCal BOOM?
Southern California Biogeochemical Ocean Observations and Models—SoCal BOOM—is an annual meeting for the regional marine-biogeochemistry community. It welcomes work spanning global and regional questions, observations, experiments, proxy records, theory, and numerical modeling.
Mission
The one-day symposium brings together students, postdoctoral researchers, researchers, and faculty from institutions across Southern California. Its goals are to:

highlight research led by graduate students and postdoctoral researchers;
foster interaction between observational and modeling communities;
support new regional collaborations; and
provide an approachable setting for sharing work in progress.

Faculty and other senior researchers are encouraged to attend, participate in discussion, and support early-career presenters.
Research community
The meeting welcomes scientists across ocean biogeochemistry, including those working in laboratories, in the field, with remote or proxy observations, and with theoretical or numerical models. Participants are encouraged to explain how their research connects measurements, mechanisms, and models of the Earth system.
The sixth annual SoCal BOOM will be held at USC on February 6, 2027.

title: Travel & Logistics
text:
Meeting location
The 2027 meeting will be held at USC’s University Park Campus. The specific building will be announced before the meeting. Check current transit schedules, fares, and parking rules when planning your trip.


Best ways to reach USC
LA public transit
Metro is usually the simplest way to reach campus without dealing with USC parking. The Metro E Line serves USC at Expo/Vermont, Expo Park/USC, and Jefferson/USC.

From Santa Monica, Culver City, and other Westside locations, take the E Line directly toward downtown Los Angeles.
From UCLA or Westwood, take a local bus, Santa Monica Big Blue Bus, or Culver CityBus connection to the E Line.
From Los Angeles Union Station, take the Metro B or D Line to 7th St/Metro Center, then transfer to the E Line.
Other Metro rail and bus routes connect with the E Line throughout Los Angeles County.

Use a TAP card or the TAP app and check Metro for the best route on the day of travel.
Intercity rail
Amtrak and Metrolink are good options for attendees traveling from outside central Los Angeles.

From Santa Barbara, Ventura, or the San Fernando Valley: use Amtrak’s Pacific Surfliner or Metrolink’s Ventura County Line.
From Orange County or San Diego: use the Pacific Surfliner or Metrolink’s Orange County Line.
From the Inland Empire and other regional locations: use the applicable Metrolink line.

Most intercity trips arrive at Los Angeles Union Station. From there, take the Metro B or D Line to 7th St/Metro Center and transfer to the E Line for USC. Train frequency varies, especially on weekends, so check schedules in advance.
Driving and parking
If you drive, use a live navigation app for the best route. Traffic near downtown Los Angeles, I-10, and I-110 can change quickly.
You have two practical parking options:
Park at USC
Visitor parking is available in USC campus structures, generally on a cashless, first-come basis. Common options include McCarthy Way, Figueroa Street, Downey Way, Royal Street, and USC Shrine. The planning estimate is approximately $20 per day, but rates and availability can change.
Check USC’s current parking instructions before arriving. Nearby street parking is limited and often metered or permit-restricted.
Park at Metro and ride in
Parking at a Metro station and taking the E Line can be cheaper and easier than driving onto campus. Metro parking is often about $3 per day, plus train fare; some lots may be free on weekends or holidays.
Useful E Line park-and-ride options west of USC include:

La Cienega/Jefferson
Culver City
Expo/Sepulveda
Expo/Bundy
Expo/Crenshaw

Travelers from other directions can park along the A or B Line and transfer to the E Line. Ride to Expo Park/USC or Jefferson/USC. Check current lot prices, hours, and availability before choosing a station.
Nearby lodging

USC Hotel is adjacent to campus.
Downtown Los Angeles and LA Live have many hotels with convenient Metro access to USC.
Koreatown and Culver City offer additional options with transit connections.

These are general suggestions, not reserved conference room blocks.

title: SoCal BOOM

About

Coming soon!
The 6th Annual Southern California Biogeochemical Ocean Observations and Models (SoCal BOOM) meeting is for global and regional marine biogeochemistry – whether you work on a ship, on a computer, or by proxy. The symposium will be held on Saturday, February 6, 2027, at the University of Southern California, from 9AM – 8PM. The meeting aims to bring together students, postdocs, researchers, and faculty from across the Southern California region interested in marine biogeochemistry.



Mission
This one-day symposium is designed to highlight the work of early-career researchers, with both the symposium and the poster session featuring presentations by graduate students and postdoctoral researchers (with faculty encouraged to attend). The aim of this meeting is to foster interaction and collaboration among oceanographers who use observations and modeling approaches to understand Earth systems. We welcome scientists engaged in a wide range of ocean biogeochemical research and encourage participants to highlight aspects of their research that draw upon theoretical or numerical modeling approaches.

title: FAQs
text:
Who is SoCal BOOM for?
The meeting is for people interested in marine biogeochemistry, including students, postdoctoral researchers, faculty, researchers, and undergraduates. The program spans observational, experimental, proxy-based, theoretical, and modeling approaches.
Who may submit an abstract?
At the 2027 meeting, oral and poster presentations were open to graduate students and postdoctoral researchers. Eligibility for the next meeting will be confirmed on the Abstracts page.
Do I need to present in order to attend?
No. Previous meetings welcomed attendees who were not presenting, including undergraduates, faculty, and other researchers.

title: For Presenters
text:
2027 presenter guidance is forthcoming
Presentation formats, timing, poster dimensions, and day-of instructions have not yet been confirmed. The information below is carried forward from the 2027 symposium as a planning reference.


Who can present?
For the 2027 symposium, oral and poster presentations were open to graduate students and postdoctoral researchers. Faculty and other researchers were encouraged to attend and participate in the discussion.
To submit work for the next meeting, see Abstracts.
Presentation opportunities
SoCal BOOM is designed to foreground early-career research. In 2027, graduate students and postdoctoral researchers could request one of three formats:

a full-length oral presentation;
a lightning talk; or
a poster presentation.

Oral presentations
Full-length talks
The 2027 program assigned each speaker a 15-minute slot: 12 minutes for the presentation and 3 minutes for questions. Speakers were asked to bring their presentation on a flash drive or send it to an organizer before the meeting.
Lightning talks
Lightning speakers received a 5-minute presentation slot. Questions were held until the end of the session so the audience could discuss the lightning talks together.
Poster presentations
The maximum poster size in 2027 was 45 × 45 inches. Both 45 × 45-inch square posters and 45 × 36-inch horizontal posters fit the supplied double-sided boards. Clips and push pins were provided.
Two poster sessions were held during the meeting. Presenters checked in at the registration table to receive a board location and were expected to attend their poster only during their assigned session.
Before the meeting
Once the current program is released, check the Schedule for your assigned talk time or poster session. Questions can be sent through Contact Us.
Source: 2027 information for presenters.
